en: If you subjugate and slaughter the people,
Your nation will surely slip from your grasp.
Hero, heed our words;
Act with restraint.
Spare the great mass of your common subjects,
Hero—the people are your treasure.
Brave Kyyaz of the Jediger
Roused and gathered the Jediger of Jeti-Özön,
Whipping them into a frenzy.
Raving, ‘I will avenge the blood-debt,’
He drove them into madness,
Drove them here in misery,
Tormenting them and raising an uproar.
He drove us here in a long column;
We gathered together only
Because he said, ‘We shall attack the gray-maned hero.’
We never desired, hero,
For the people to be slaughtered.
As we set out for this place,
The birches fell and the willows wept.
‘We shall die if we face the bloodthirsty man!’
All the common people cried.
White-bearded old men wept,
Saying, ‘Now we shall be left without fathers’;
Children old enough to speak wept.
Brave Kyyaz’s oppression,
His countless acts of violence, fell upon us.
Women wept in grief;
We Jediger were herded here,
Despairing of our precious lives.
My prince, look upon us and heed our words.
If you do not believe these words,
You are the lion and we are sheep—
Then slaughter us outright.
If you believe no traitor lives among the people,
Then heed these words of mine:
Against Kyyaz of the Jediger,
Hero, wage single combat.
Tootoru, the swift horse ready for battle,
Is a racer famed for vanquishing nations;
Hero, take him as your prize.
Spare the innocent-hearted people;
Your foe to fight is brave Kyyaz.
Hero, face him in combat and see.
Against Kyyaz, ablaze with deadly fury,
Shout and level your spear.
Show your fearsome strength and valor
Against brave Kyyaz.
Since it was Kyyaz who stirred up the conflict,
If you attack these peaceful people,
It will bring you shame.
Brave Kyyaz of the Jediger
Is not nobler-born than you;
Look, hero, his courage is no greater than yours.
Roar and drive in your spear;
You are the heroic lion Choro—
From wrathful Kyyaz’s hand
Deliver us.”
So Kadyrbay
Sharpened his eloquent tongue
And poured out his heartfelt speech.
Finding Kadyrbay’s words just,
The army clamored and raised an uproar.
If only they had found a way,
The distressed people, surging in anger,
Would have attacked Kyyaz themselves.
They crossed a ridge
Shaped like the back of a saddle;
Many who could find no other way
Fled and reached that place.
Escaping, they went to Kyyaz
And brought him the news.
After thrusting their spears in fury,
The Jediger, for the time it takes meat to cook,
Were left unable to speak,
Grieving in distress.
Many men led by Tölöbay—
Tölöbay, son of Tölök,
And Kadyrbay, son of Kalcha—
Men skilled upon the field of combat,
Broad-mouthed and high-browed,
Eloquent men who gladdened the soul,
Capable men hurrying in alarm—
Before brave Kyyaz
Those strong men fled in dismay.
The people rushed about in panic and turmoil;
Before brave Kyyaz
They went and began to speak:
“Here, take your spear!” they said.
Amid the people’s clamor, they cast
His spear before brave Kyyaz.
Kadyrbay, son of Kalcha,
Spoke fully and held nothing back:
“Jeti-Suu is the land where you dwell;
From Jeti-Suu you raised an army,
A vast host that shook the earth.
You enlisted grim-hearted champions,
Warriors who never retreat.
It seems we came to endure
Great turmoil and terrible calamity;
It seems we came to die
At the hands of the bloodthirsty lion himself.
Assailing one blessed by Kydyr,
We became needlessly entangled in slaughter;
Assailing a lion-hearted champion,
We became needlessly entangled with death.
It seems we came to witness
Unbounded turmoil and great calamity.
I put my trust in Kanchoro,
But your Kanchoro is a runaway slave;
It seems we came today to die
At the hands of the bloodthirsty lion.
Understand well the worth of peace.
You who rule Jeti-Suu,
Who would surrender your comrade to no one
And never yielded weeping before an enemy—
You were a panther; remember that.
Ill-fated Kyyaz, heed my words.
The army has gone mad and seethes;
The people clamor and the nation is in turmoil.
He has come to have them gathered;
That fawning madman has come
To have every one of these people
Slaughtered.
Külchoro is a bullet already fired;
Your boastful ally Kanchoro
Has no gift for diplomacy.
Let us select countless swift steeds
And offer them to the bloodthirsty hero.
Let the Jediger cease their frenzy,
And return without a massacre.
If Külchoro comes surging in fury,
He will do whatever he pleases.
If Semetey grows wrathful,
He will slaughter every last person.
Külchoro would reap their midst
As though cutting grain with a sickle.
Not merely the Jediger, but the whole world—
Not merely the Kyrgyz, but all mankind,
Not merely mankind, but Rome itself—
If the gray-maned hero rose in wrath,
He would swallow them all, leaving none.
If angered, he could chew up
The old men and spit them out.
Hero, this panther Semetey
Could devour all the Jediger;
His brow seems broad enough to bar the sky,
As though he could swallow all he sees.
His silhouette is like a cliff with an overhanging crest,
His strength like tempered blue steel.
He seems able to devour whoever strikes at him;
Every limb is like a tiger’s,
And none who grapples with him survives.
I climbed a ridge and braced myself,
And saw the champion’s figure
Towering like a lofty snow-white mountain.
That gray-maned hero’s valor
Is found in no other man.
I searched, but that formidable man’s courage
Is found nowhere among the people.
Ah, the valor of that noble-hearted lord!
Born for these Kyrgyz,
He is a fortress of tempered blue steel.
Against the infidel hordes like black beetles,
It was fitting that he slaughter their people
And opened the road through Beijing.
Through Chinmachin and Kakan
It was fitting that he opened a road;
Slaughtering their frenzied Kalmak champions
And destroying their warriors,
It was fitting that he went there;
It was fitting that he brought
A murderous battle upon the Chinese.
From terrible disaster and calamity
He truly delivered
The Kyrgyz people.
I saw Semetey
And lost my wits and senses;
Unable to find a way, I panicked—
My body trembling and my senses gone,
I fled to you, brave Kyyaz.
I saw Semetey:
High-eared and handsome of face.
If you catch word of that black-fated killer,
Flee far away.
Like a ravenous lion or tiger,
He is a man poised to seize his prey;
Like a true tusked boar,
He is a warrior poised to strike.
Born for the whole wide world,
He appears like the constellation Ülkör;
He seems like the pillar
That props up the sky.
When you see that formidable man,
Your heart is torn apart.
He seems like the unstoppable
Tempest of the whole wide world.
When stirred, he can make the world heave;
To the vast multitudes of Kyrgyz,
To the flourishing Kyrgyz nation,
He seems a father.
He is the dark, watchful eye
Of all courageous champions;
He is the very lion
Who leads the nation and guards the people.
No living soul can face his wrath;
Of those who grapple with the hero
Who protects his people, none remains alive.
With one ear standing high,
As if guarding a valley like a ridge,
He could drain anyone who fought him
More readily than he would crush a fly.
I saw the message of the murderer
The nose is like a whole mountain
Like swallowing a bubble,
The head is like a mountain,
Let's get started
Just like eating.
A soul appeared under it
The cause of death:
There are six thousand types of men
I look back
Sixty thousand citizens
Piers of white blue sky
As if reaching the bottom,
Aiza was stretching
Now it's like drinking
Black streak
Lying on the side
He stood like a mule,
He saw the bottom and rested.
There are six thousand types of wrestlers,
He saw the bottom and came out alive.
Now a devourer
There is a type of dragon.
Beren faced the lion,
Let's get to the grave
Jurgun Kiyaz, let's go.
Separated from the crowd,
Let's not be a part,
The population is running and dying.
Let's not die.
Do not watch the carnage with interest
Do not grow mustaches,
Our Kyrgyz head,
Does not die for nothing from China?
Hiding in the darkness,
Encountered by an evil ghost,
Let's not die badly?
Black blood came from the lungs,
Shivering in a hurry,
Hissing from the tumult,
Let's not die badly?
Jaketai made us slaves.
Death has come and gone,
Black blood came out of my throat,
